_comment: Source and artifact provenance for every committed circuit trusted-setup artifact. Hashes are real sha256sum output taken 2026-11-13, not generated figures. 'last_touched_commit' is git log -1 --format=%H -- <path> against that exact file, not the circuit source or this manifest's own commit.
trusted_setup_disclosure: circuits/build.sh states directly: 'THIS IS A DEV CEREMONY: single local contributor, /dev/urandom entropy. Every artifact this produces is suitable for testnet/development use only.' Every zkey/verification_key.json below was produced by that script. A production ceremony with multiple independent contributors is required before any of these artifacts are trusted with real value — see docs/EXTERNAL_AUDIT_PREPARATION.md and the trusted-setup finding in docs/ZKELLA_VS_OPENZEPPELIN_TECHNICAL_COMPARISON.md Section C.5.

phase1_ptau_source.claimed_origin: Hermez/Polygon public Powers-of-Tau ceremony, per circuits/build.sh's own header comment: https://hermez.s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/powersOfTau28_hez_final_<N>.ptau
phase1_ptau_source.verification_status: NOT independently re-verified in this pass against Hermez's own published ptau hashes. The local files' sha256 is recorded below for future cross-checking; treat the 'claimed_origin' as what the build script asserts, not as independently confirmed provenance.

.ptau/pot13_final.ptau.status: present, appears valid (correct magnitude for a real ptau file)

.ptau/pot16_final.ptau.status: present, appears valid (correct magnitude for a real ptau file)

.ptau/pot12_final.ptau.status: FIXED (2026-11-13). Was a 263-byte S3 'AccessDenied' XML error response saved to disk instead of a real ptau file (confirmed: re-requesting the exact URL circuits/build.sh's header cites, https://hermez.s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/powersOfTau28_hez_final_12.ptau, now returns a live HTTP 403 from the same bucket — the bucket itself no longer serves this file publicly, which is almost certainly how the corrupted copy was produced in the first place and why re-downloading it is not a durable fix). Regenerated locally instead, using the same single-contributor /dev/urandom dev-ceremony pattern already used for pot13/pot16 (`snarkjs powersoftau new bn128 12` -> `contribute` -> `prepare phase2`), then verified with `snarkjs powersoftau verify` (passes) and with two real from-scratch circuit builds through circuits/build.sh (shield, 1264 constraints, and compliance/non_membership, 17533 constraints -- the latter to confirm the loop still falls through correctly past pot12 when a circuit needs a larger file). Both succeeded end to end and their output was discarded (not committed) since they used fresh, different dev-ceremony randomness than the already-audited, already-committed zkeys below. .ptau/ is gitignored (*.ptau in .gitignore), so this file is local-only and was not re-downloaded from, or compared against, any public ceremony transcript -- same dev-only caveat as every other artifact in this file.

shield.phase2_contribution: ZKELLA dev contribution (circuits/build.sh's fixed --name= value), /dev/urandom entropy, one non-interactive contribution
shield.ptau_used: pot12_final.ptau at build time (912 and 1264-constraint circuits fall under build.sh's first 2^12 threshold check) — the originally-used file is gone (superseded by a different corrupted-then-regenerated copy, see phase1_ptau_source above); this committed zkey/VK were not rebuilt and are unaffected either way
shield.cross_checked_against_live_testnet: yes — this exact verification_key.json's encoding matches the VK registered on-chain for CircuitType::Shield on the live testnet_final verifier contract, confirmed byte-for-byte during this engagement's earlier live-Testnet audit pass (see docs/OPENZEPPELIN_BENCHMARK_COMPARISON.md section 11)

unshield.phase2_contribution: ZKELLA dev contribution, /dev/urandom entropy, one non-interactive contribution
unshield.ptau_used: pot16_final.ptau (10605 constraints needs 2^14 at minimum; no pot14/pot15 file present locally, so build.sh's loop falls through to the next available file, pot16) — confirmed still valid and present

transfer_2in2out.ptau_used: pot16_final.ptau (21391 constraints needs 2^15 at minimum; no pot15 present, falls through to pot16) — confirmed still valid and present

swap_fairness.phase2_contribution: ZKELLA dev contribution, /dev/urandom entropy, one non-interactive contribution, rebuilt 2026-10-13 for the min_amount_out binding fix
swap_fairness.ptau_used: pot12_final.ptau at build time — confirmed still valid as of this circuit's 2026-10-13 rebuild (the D3 min_amount_out fix), since the rebuild succeeded; the file was corrupted between then and this review but has since been regenerated (fixed 2026-11-13, see phase1_ptau_source above) — this committed zkey/VK were not rebuilt and are unaffected either way
swap_fairness.cross_checked_against_live_testnet: yes — this circuit's VK is the one live on testnet_final's verifier contract for CircuitType::SwapFairness; a real cross-asset swap lifecycle using it is recorded in docs/TRANCHE2_DELIVERABLES.md section 3

toolchain_versions_used_to_produce_this_.note: These are the versions installed in this review's environment, used only to re-derive constraint counts (snarkjs r1cs info) for cross-checking — not necessarily the exact versions used when each artifact was originally built. No tracked circom/snarkjs version pin exists in this repository today; see HYG01 (contracts/rust-toolchain.toml) for the equivalent fix already applied on the Rust side. A circom/snarkjs version pin for circuit rebuilds is a reasonable follow-up, not done in this pass.
